name: PayPal
summary: PayPal runs online payments and digital wallets for consumers and merchants, including Venmo and Braintree. Its careers site describes a recruiter call followed by interviews with team members, and suggests reviewing its core values and Leadership Principles before you interview. For engineering roles, candidates commonly report an online coding assessment, then coding, system design and behavioural interviews.
rounds: Recruiter call about the role and your experience
Online coding assessment for many engineering and intern roles
Team interviews, often several: coding, system design for experienced roles, and behavioural
Hiring manager interview on your past work and the competencies for the role
Recruiter follow-up on next steps and any offer
looks_for: Care for security, reliability and correctness when money is involved

questions.text: Tell me about a time you started from a customer's most pressing need and worked back to a solution.
covers: How you found out what the customer needed most
The options you considered and why you chose one
The result for the customer, with a number if you have one

questions.text: Tell me about a time you took ownership of a problem that crossed team lines.
covers: Why nobody owned it and what it was costing
How you brought the teams together and agreed who does what
The outcome and how ownership was settled afterwards

questions.text: Tell me about a time you helped a colleague grow or do their best work.
covers: Who they were and what was holding them back
What you did: feedback, coaching, giving them a chance to lead
How they grew, and what you learned about helping others

questions.text: Tell me about a time you had to move fast without lowering quality.
covers: The deadline and why speed mattered
What you simplified and what you refused to cut, such as tests or security checks
The result and anything you fixed afterwards

questions.text: How would you make sure a customer is never charged twice if a payment request is retried?
covers: An idempotency key sent with each payment request
Storing the key with the result so a retry returns the same answer
Timeouts and partial failures between your service and the bank

questions.text: How would you design a system that flags risky payments in real time without blocking good customers?
covers: Signals: device, location, amount, history, how fast payments arrive
Rules plus a scoring model, with a fast path and a review path
Measuring both missed fraud and wrongly blocked customers

questions.text: Explain how you'd keep account balances correct when many transactions hit the same account at once.
covers: Transactions and locking, or a ledger of entries rather than editing a balance
Avoiding race conditions and lost updates
Reconciling against the ledger to catch errors

questions.text: Payment failures in one country are higher than usual this morning. How would you find out why?
covers: Splitting failures by payment method, bank, app version and error code
Checking recent releases, partner outages and rule changes
Protecting customers first, then fixing and explaining the cause

questions.text: What happens, step by step, when someone pays a merchant online with a card or a wallet?
covers: Checkout, authorisation by the issuer, then capture
The parties involved: merchant, payment processor, card network, banks
Settlement later, plus refunds and disputes

questions.text: Walk me through a service you built: how it handled failures, and how you'd make it more reliable.
covers: What the service did and who depended on it
A real failure and how the system or team responded
Changes you'd make: retries, timeouts, monitoring, graceful fallbacks

questions.text: Why PayPal, and what do you think makes people trust a payments company?
covers: A reason tied to PayPal's products or customers
What builds trust: security, reliability, fair handling of problems
How your work would add to that trust

questions.text: Which PayPal value or Leadership Principle fits how you work, and why?
covers: One value or principle, named once
A short, specific example from your work
Why it matters to you

questions.text: Where would you like to grow in the next few years, and how would this role help?
covers: One or two specific skills or responsibilities
How this role builds them
What you'd contribute in return

tips: PayPal's interviewing page suggests reviewing its company values, its Leadership Principles and the job description before you interview.
Give a specific, detailed example for each competency, and draw examples from more than one job or project, as PayPal's own checklist suggests.
For payments design questions, talk about retries, duplicate charges, fraud and audit trails, not only speed.
Interviews are usually by video; test your setup beforehand and keep your camera on, which PayPal says it prefers.

sources.title: PayPal mission, values and Leadership Principles (about.pypl.com)
